title: Computer-use models will agentify the web, not APIs — Dhruv Batra, Yutori
talk_summary: Dhruv Batra argues that the long tail of the web will not expose APIs or MCP servers, so agents must operate on pixels (screenshots in, clicks/scrolls out), optionally writing JS on demand, with the screenshot as ground truth. He cites Navigator N1.5 at 97% human-eval on Mind2Web and ~$0.80 vs $2.30 per task versus frontier models, and proposes orchestrators launching many parallel browser sandboxes.

takeaways.technique: Orchestrator fan-out over parallel sandboxed workers
takeaways.what_they_do: An orchestrator launches multiple worker agents in parallel, each in its own cloud sandbox, so throughput exceeds what one sequential agent can do.

takeaways.technique: Small specialized model beats frontier on cost/latency at equal accuracy
takeaways.what_they_do: They use a smaller-footprint model that matches frontier accuracy on their benchmark but is much faster and cheaper per multi-step task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're looking at 80 cents per task versus $2.30, and that makes a big difference

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent writes small JS functions to act on the page in bulk, but verifies success from the rendered screenshot rather than trusting the code path.
takeaways.evidence_quote: click buttons when you have to, write code when you have to, and look at the result uh through pixels

takeaways.technique: Retire saturated benchmarks, build harder ones
takeaways.what_they_do: When a benchmark hits ~97% they stop trusting it and construct harder multi-step tasks instead of celebrating the score.
takeaways.evidence_quote: At this point of time, you should just retire the benchmark, build something harder.

takeaways.what_they_do: Each parallel worker gets its own cloud sandbox instance rather than sharing a host.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each with a cloud cloud sandbox instance
